subject: Unexpected throttling during Evergrow campaign — suspected burst-window interlock misconfig
messages:
From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@evergrow.health>
To: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom West <tom.west@evergrow.health>
Date: Tue, 29 Jul 2025 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production throttling during 08:00 UTC campaign window

Hi Neha,

We experienced significant throttling and 429s from Redwood between 08:02–09:55 UTC during our scheduled promotional campaign. Our telemetry shows a spike to ~25% 429 responses and median token latency climbed from ~220ms to ~1.8s. The error spike disproportionately affected longer chat sessions (seq len >1024).

Attached: evergrow_metrics_2025-07-29.csv and a screenshot of 429s (support_screenshot_429.png). This caused our campaign messages to delay or drop and impacted ~18k end users.

Can you confirm whether this is an upstream capacity issue or a configuration problem on your side? We need an ETA for mitigation and are asking for credits for the impacted window.

Thanks,
Alice Chen
Head of Integrations — Evergrow Health
alice.chen@evergrow.health

From: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@evergrow.health>, Tom West <tom.west@evergrow.health>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 29 Jul 2025 08:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production throttling during 08:00 UTC campaign window

Thanks Alice — I'm very sorry for the disruption. I'm escalating this immediately and looping in ops and infra. High level: we see signs of policy-level throttling rather than capacity exhaustion (initial metrics match a burst-window interlock we rolled out last week).

Immediate asks from our side:
- Can you share the exact campaign request window (start/end) and one representative request id from the CSV?
- Please confirm if you were pinned to a specific model variant during the campaign.

Planned immediate mitigation (we'll confirm after infra triage):
1) Temporarily increase per-tenant burst allowance for Evergrow and enable a conservative fallback to the legacy serving policy.
2) Roll back the burst-window interlock in the affected pool if the root cause points to that config.
3) Provide a full timeline and a postmortem + credit proposal.

We're treating this as a P1 because it impacted customer traffic and will escalate to execs if SLA exposure >1 hour. I'll update within 30 minutes.

Neha Kapoor
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Phone: +1 (415) 555-6123

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: Alice Chen <alice.chen@evergrow.health>
Date: Tue, 29 Jul 2025 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production throttling during 08:00 UTC campaign window

On Tue, Jul 29, 2025 at 08:25 AM PDT, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai wrote:
> Thanks Alice — I'm very sorry for the disruption. I'm escalating this immediately and looping in ops and infra. High level: we see signs of policy-level throttling rather than capacity exhaustion (initial metrics match a burst-window interlock we rolled out last week).

Quick root cause summary from infra triage (initial):
- We deployed a change to burst-credit interlock logic in pool 'us-west-2-burst-pool' on 2025-07-28 22:11 UTC. The change ties tenant burst credits to global safety valve state.
- For tenants pinned to the new fast-path serving mode, the refill-rate for burst credits was effectively halved for short windows (burst_window=60s but refill_rate scaled x0.5). That causes a credit exhaustion pattern under short, high QPS bursts and results in deterministic 429s until the window resets.
- The automated fallback that should have routed to the legacy serving policy did not activate because the tenant's model variant string included a suffix that our routing rules didn't match. (Mismatch: fast-path=="v2-opt" vs fallback rule expecting "v2".)

Planned immediate actions (executing now):
- Revert the interlock in the affected pool to restore previous refill semantics.
- Apply a temporary per-tenant burst override for Evergrow: +2x burst allowance for 2 hours.
- Patch routing rule to ensure fallback triggers when model variant includes suffixes (hotfix to be deployed to edge at 09:20 UTC).

I've attached policy_snapshot_v2.json with the config diff. Will report back with metric deltas after the fixes.

-Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, Alice Chen <alice.chen@evergrow.health>
Date: Tue, 29 Jul 2025 12:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production throttling during 08:00 UTC campaign window

On Tue, Jul 29, 2025 at 09:05 AM PDT, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai wrote:
> Planned immediate actions (executing now):
> - Revert the interlock in the affected pool to restore previous refill semantics.
> - Apply a temporary per-tenant burst override for Evergrow: +2x burst allowance for 2 hours.
> - Patch routing rule to ensure fallback triggers when model variant includes suffixes (hotfix to be deployed to edge at 09:20 UTC).

Update from ops (what we did at 12:30 PDT local):
- Rolled back the burst-credit interlock in us-west-2-burst-pool (deployed and validated).
- Applied per-tenant burst override for tenant evergrow:burst_override=200%. Effective immediately for next 2 hours.
- Deployed routing hotfix to edge; fallback now matches variant suffixes and we've added a guard to force legacy routing if burst credit consumption >80% for 2 consecutive windows.

Observed impact: within 12 minutes of the rollback + override we see 429 rate drop from ~25% -> ~1.6% and p95 token latency back to ~320ms. Attached screenshot and metrics (evergrow_metrics_2025-07-29.csv) for your review.

Next steps / asks for Evergrow:
- Can you validate whether your campaign webhook retries behaved as expected after 12:40 UTC?
- We'll keep the override for 2 hours and then reduce to a conservative headroom while we push a permanent config change.

Jonas Weber
Senior Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai

From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@evergrow.health>
To: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom West <tom.west@evergrow.health>, ProcOps <procurement@evergrow.health>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 29 Jul 2025 14:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production throttling during 08:00 UTC campaign window

Thanks for the quick follow and the hotfix. We validated our retry logs and saw delivery rates return to normal after 12:45 UTC. That said, the outage window lasted ~2 hours for our users and caused immediate ROI impact for today's campaign — we estimate ~$18k in lost conversions and extra engineering hours on our side.

Requesting next items:
- Formal postmortem and timeline for permanent config change (we need assurance that future burst-window changes won't silently flip our traffic to 429s).
- A credit proposal for the impacted window and documentation of the routing hotfix.
- Steps we should take on our side to detect this earlier (alerting hints or headers we can watch).

Appreciate the responsiveness — please escalate this to leadership for credit approval and permanent mitigations.

Best,
Alice
